card.summary: S. 2805 requires the U.S. Secretary of State to submit a report to Congress within 60 days of enactment determining whether Ukrainian children kidnapped, deported, or forcibly removed by the Russian Federation since February 2022 have been safely reunited with their families and are reintegrating into Ukrainian society. If the Secretary cannot certify these reunifications and reintegrations, the bill requires the Secretary to immediately designate the Russian Federation as a state sponsor of terrorism under specified U.S. laws.

summary: S. 2978 requires the Secretary of State to submit a report to Congress within 60 days of the bill's effective date certifying specific conditions regarding the actions of the Russian Federation. If the Secretary of State cannot certify that all listed conditions are met—including the safe return and reintegration of displaced Ukrainian children and the cessation of attacks on civilians and infrastructure—the Secretary must immediately designate the Russian Federation as a state sponsor of terrorism.

affected_groups.effect: Must submit a formal certification report to Congress within 60 days and potentially designate the Russian Federation as a state sponsor of terrorism.
Subject to a potential designation as a state sponsor of terrorism and protection of its blocked sovereign assets from certain U.S. court judgments.
Directly impacts conditions surrounding the repatriation, reunification, and reintegration of children displaced since February 2022.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of State to submit a report to Congress within 60 days of the effective date to certify whether Ukrainian children taken since February 2022 have been safely reunited with their families.
Requires the certification report to determine if the full reintegration of those children into Ukrainian society is underway.

Requires the certification report to determine whether the Russian government has ceased attacks on European civilian infrastructure and assassination attempts, as well as all attacks on civilians and infrastructure in Ukraine.

Mandates that if the Secretary of State cannot certify all required conditions, the Secretary must immediately designate the Russian Federation as a state sponsor of terrorism under specified provisions of law.
Establishes conditions and a 45-day waiting period after certification under which the Secretary of State may rescind the designation.
Prohibits blocked or immobilized Russian sovereign assets from being subject to attachment or execution of any judgment entered by a U.S. court against Russia arising from this designation.
missing_information: Specific details regarding the exact procedural mechanisms the Secretary of State must use for the certification beyond the statutory references.
Information on how other federal agencies will alter their enforcement mechanisms upon designation.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 2978 requires the Secretary of State to submit a report to Congress within 60 days of the bill's effective date certifying specific conditions regarding the actions of the Russian Federation. If the Secretary of State cannot certify that all listed conditions are met—including the safe return and reintegration of displaced Ukrainian children and the cessation of attacks on civilians and infrastructure—the Secretary must immediately designate the Russian Federation as a state sponsor of terrorism.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs U.S. foreign policy actions regarding the formal designation of a major world power as a state sponsor of terrorism based on specific geopolitical events, military actions, and the treatment of displaced children in Ukraine.
